questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which author presentation opening is strongest?

answer.text: A. My piece has a lot of things in it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and does not frame the audience.

answer.text: B. "Halfway Home" is a short poem meant to show a speaker deciding whether to return or move forward.

feedback.text: Correct. This names title, form, and purpose. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I will explain every line before you read it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This overexplains and may replace the creative work.

answer.text: D. The piece is finished, so no explanation matters.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A presentation should prepare the audience. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

What is craft reasoning?

answer.text: A. Listing every event in the plot.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Plot summary is not craft reasoning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Saying the piece is good.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain a specific choice.

answer.text: C. Reading the title only.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Craft reasoning requires explanation. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Explaining why a writer made a specific choice and how it affects the reader.

feedback.text: Correct. This defines craft reasoning. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which sentence best explains a craft choice?

answer.text: A. I used short sentences during the argument so the scene would feel tense and quick.

feedback.text: Correct. This names the choice and explains reader effect.

answer.text: B. I wrote sentences because writing needs sentences.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. My piece has punctuation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain why the punctuation matters.

answer.text: D. I like my story.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is personal opinion, not craft reasoning.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which presentation should be revised because it is mostly summary?

answer.text: A. I wanted the poem to show hesitation, so I used pauses before the final line.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This explains purpose and craft. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I revised the ending after feedback because the first version explained too much.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This explains revision. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. First the character walks, then talks, then thinks, then goes home, and that is the whole story.

feedback.text: Correct. This retells events without craft reasoning. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: D. As you read, notice the repeated hallway image.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This frames the audience. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which audience frame is strongest?

answer.text: A. Notice everything and nothing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I will tell you the ending before you read.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This may replace the reading experience. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Ignore the images.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not support craft understanding. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. As you read, notice how the repeated hallway image changes from safety to pressure.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives the audience a specific craft feature to notice.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

A student says, "I revised because the teacher said to." What is missing?

answer.text: A. A longer plot summary.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The issue is revision reasoning, not plot summary.

answer.text: B. An explanation of what changed and why the final version is stronger.

feedback.text: Correct. Revision reflection must explain improvement. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: C. A random new title.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A title does not solve missing revision reasoning.

answer.text: D. A list of every comma.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The problem is not just conventions. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which revision reflection is strongest?

answer.text: A. I cut the first paragraph because it explained the conflict before the reader could experience it.

feedback.text: Correct. This names a change and explains the effect.

answer.text: B. I changed things randomly.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not show purposeful revision. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I did not read the feedback.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That does not show revision reflection. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. I added more words because more is always better.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Length alone does not prove improvement. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which presentation order best matches the lesson?

answer.text: A. Ending, unrelated memory, no title, no purpose.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not guide the audience. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Full plot summary, every symbol, no revision.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This overexplains and misses revision reflection. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Title and form, purpose, craft choices, revision decision, audience frame.

feedback.text: Correct. This is the lesson's presentation sequence.

answer.text: D. Font choice only.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Font choice alone is not an author presentation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which statement best keeps the creative work central?

answer.text: A. I will explain every possible meaning before anyone reads.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This replaces the creative work. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. There is no need to read the piece after my presentation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The presentation should support reading. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. My summary is more important than the poem.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The creative work should remain central. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. I will point the audience to the repeated image, then let the poem create its own effect.

feedback.text: Correct. This guides the audience without replacing the work.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which choice is a useful craft choice to explain?

answer.text: A. Point of view, because it shapes what the reader knows and feels.

feedback.text: Correct. Point of view is a meaningful craft choice.

answer.text: B. The fact that the page exists.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not a specific craft choice.

answer.text: C. The writer's lunch.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is unrelated. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. A random file name.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain the creative work.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

A student says, "My poem is about sadness." How can this purpose statement be improved?

answer.text: A. Make it longer by listing every line.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Length does not necessarily improve purpose. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Explain the specific effect, such as showing sadness through ordinary objects rather than direct statements.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives a clearer intended effect. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Remove the purpose entirely.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Purpose helps frame the presentation. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Replace it with "I do not know."

feedback.text: Incorrect. That does not frame the audience. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which response best explains an author's title choice?

answer.text: A. I picked the title randomly.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not show craft reasoning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Titles never matter.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Titles can prepare the audience. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I used the title to avoid revising.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A title does not replace revision. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. I chose "Open Door" because the door image represents both invitation and uncertainty.

feedback.text: Correct. This explains the title's effect. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which is not enough for mastery in this lesson?

answer.text: A. A presentation that names purpose and form.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That supports mastery. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. A presentation that explains two craft choices.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That supports mastery. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. A presentation that only says "I like my piece."

feedback.text: Correct. This lacks purpose, craft reasoning, and revision reflection.

answer.text: D. A presentation that reflects on revision.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That supports mastery. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which sentence best connects feedback to revision?

answer.text: A. Peer feedback showed the ending was too direct, so I replaced the explanation with an action that suggests the feeling.

feedback.text: Correct. This explains feedback, revision, and effect. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I ignored all feedback.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not connect feedback to improvement.

answer.text: C. Feedback exists.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too vague. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. I changed the whole piece because someone spoke.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not show thoughtful revision. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which presentation language is clearest and most author-focused?

answer.text: A. Stuff happened and I wrote it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I used first-person narration so the reader would experience the speaker's uncertainty directly.

feedback.text: Correct. This explains a craft choice and reader effect.

answer.text: C. It is whatever you think.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This avoids author reasoning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. I cannot explain anything.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The lesson requires explanation. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

What should an author presentation avoid?

answer.text: A. Naming the form.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Naming the form is useful. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Explaining a revision decision.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That is expected. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Giving an audience frame.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That helps the audience enter the piece.

answer.text: D. Overexplaining every symbol so the audience has no interpretive work left.

feedback.text: Correct. The presentation should guide, not replace, the creative work.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which reflection focuses on product and process?

answer.text: A. I finished.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain process or product.

answer.text: B. Writing happened.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too vague. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I changed the pacing after feedback, and the final version creates more tension before the reveal.

feedback.text: Correct. This connects process to final product. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: D. My draft exists.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This lacks reflection. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which author statement best explains line breaks?

answer.text: A. I broke the final phrase onto its own line so the reader would pause before the speaker's decision.

feedback.text: Correct. This explains format and reader effect. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I used line breaks because poems have lines.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain a specific effect.

answer.text: C. I added lines randomly.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random choices are not strong craft reasoning.

answer.text: D. I removed all structure.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain purposeful line breaks.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

What should the author do if the presentation becomes too long because it summarizes every event?

answer.text: A. Add more summary.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Summary is already the problem. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Focus on purpose, two craft choices, and one revision decision.

feedback.text: Correct. This brings the presentation back to the lesson sequence.

answer.text: C. Remove all craft reasoning.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Craft reasoning is required. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Avoid mentioning the creative work at all.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The presentation should still frame the work.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which sentence is the best revision of "My story is good"?

answer.text: A. My story is good because it is good.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is circular and vague. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. My story is good, and that is all.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This lacks craft reasoning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. My story has pages.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain quality. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. The repeated door image helps show the character's hesitation, especially in the final paragraph.

feedback.text: Correct. This replaces vague judgment with craft evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which element belongs in the checkpoint task?

answer.text: A. Two craft explanations with reader effects.

feedback.text: Correct. This is part of the author presentation plan.

answer.text: B. Private personal information.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That is not required and may be inappropriate.

answer.text: C. A full summary of every event only.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Summary alone is not enough. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. A peer's name as the main point.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The focus is author reasoning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which statement best shows audience awareness?

answer.text: A. I do not care what readers notice.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Audience awareness matters. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I will hide the purpose from everyone.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The presentation should frame the audience. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. As you read, notice how the sound details become quieter as the speaker calms down.

feedback.text: Correct. This guides readers to a craft pattern.

answer.text: D. The audience should not read the piece.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The presentation supports reading. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which is the best reason to mention revision in an author presentation?

answer.text: A. To prove the first draft was bad.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Revision is about improvement, not shame. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. To show how a purposeful change improved the final work.

feedback.text: Correct. This connects process and product. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: C. To avoid explaining craft.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Revision does not replace craft reasoning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. To make the presentation longer for no reason.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Length is not the goal. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which presentation response should receive corrective feedback?

answer.text: A. I used dialogue to show conflict without explaining it directly.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is strong craft reasoning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I revised the ending so the final image carries the emotion.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a useful revision explanation. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I cannot name a purpose, craft choice, or revision decision.

feedback.text: Correct. This misses the required components. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: D. As you read, notice how the hallway image changes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a useful audience frame. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which mastery response best fits Lesson 6?

answer.text: A. My presentation only retells the plot.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Plot summary alone is not enough. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. My presentation says nothing about craft.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Craft reasoning is required. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. My presentation avoids revision because revision is private.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Revision reflection is part of the lesson.

answer.text: D. My presentation names the title and form, explains the purpose, describes two craft choices, and reflects on one revision decision.

feedback.text: Correct. This includes the core mastery components. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.
